headline: OpenAI Model Disproves 80-Year-Old Geometry Problem Autonomously
summary: An internal OpenAI reasoning model has found a disproof for the Erdős unit distance problem, a conjecture that has remained unsolved for eight decades. External mathematicians have validated the finding.
details: OpenAI has reported that an internal general-purpose reasoning model autonomously disproved the Erdős unit distance problem, an open question in discrete geometry that had stood for roughly 80 years. This marks a significant application of AI to frontier research.

The internal model was not specifically trained for mathematics, according to OpenAI. External mathematicians have validated the result, confirming the disproof of this long-standing conjecture. The company has not identified the model as Astra, nor confirmed claims of it solving 10 major open problems.

The significance of this announcement lies in the age of the problem and OpenAI's account that the model worked autonomously. The confirmed development is specific: an internal model found a disproof, resolving the conjecture by showing it to be false.

OpenAI frames this work as a milestone for AI-assisted frontier research, highlighting a research capability rather than a commercial release. No information on model availability, API access, pricing, or a release date has been provided.

The achievement illustrates a direction where reasoning systems may increasingly contribute to difficult research and technical work, provided outputs can be independently checked. Organizations are advised to maintain human review in AI-assisted workflows.

Key follow-up questions include whether OpenAI will provide further technical details about the internal model, if the proof or validation process becomes more accessible, and if this research capability will be turned into an announced product. None of these outcomes are established by the reported result.

headline: Google Search time filter reportedly broken for days, users notice
summary: A crucial search tool for filtering results by date has stopped working, with the issue going unnoticed by many.
details: The time filter in Google Search, a feature allowing users to narrow down results by date, has reportedly been broken for several days. This functionality is essential for finding recent information, and its malfunction could significantly impact search accuracy for time-sensitive queries.

Users on platforms like Hacker News have begun to notice the issue, expressing surprise that such a fundamental tool could fail without widespread public outcry. The exact cause of the malfunction and the duration it has been affecting search results remain unclear.

The image provided shows the dropdown menu for the time filter, with 'Past week' highlighted, indicating a user attempting to select a time range. The absence of a checkmark or any indication of selection suggests the filter may not be applying correctly.

While Google has not yet officially commented on the issue, the lack of immediate attention to such a core search feature is concerning. This incident highlights the reliance users place on Google's search capabilities and the potential impact of even minor functional failures.
